issues.detail: The Vietnamese translation 'không có nhà tiên tri nào lớn hơn' (no prophet is greater) implies a general statement about all prophets. The Greek 'μειζων εν γεννητοις γυναικων προφητης ιωαννου' specifies that John is greater than any *other* of the children of women (i.e., among those born of human mothers). The Vietnamese phrasing loses the specific contrast between natural birth and spiritual status.

The Vietnamese 'kẻ rất nhỏ' (the very small/least) is a slightly imprecise rendering of 'ο δε μικροτερος' (the least/smallest one). While acceptable, the primary issue remains the structural shift in the first clause regarding the scope of John's greatness.
